description: hexa adr features lists every feature the decisions name, with where each stands

specs.description: A Features table gives one row per feature, with its sentence and its phase
specs.given: an accepted ADR ADR-1 titled 'Impact' with phases R1 and R2, and a `## Features` section whose table has the rows `| Blast radius | Says what goes down with a device | R2 |` and `| Impact list | Lists the affected services | |`
specs.then: declared is true; two features: 'Blast radius' with what 'Says what goes down with a device' and phases ["R2"], and 'Impact list' with what 'Lists the affected services' and phases []; each has adr 'ADR-1', adr_title 'Impact' and declared true

specs.description: Column names match without regard to case, `What` stands for `What it does`, and a row may name several phases
specs.given: an ADR with phases R1, R2 and R3 whose table header is `| feature | WHAT | phase |` and one row `| Trace | Follows a cable | R1, R3 |`
specs.then: one feature 'Trace' with what 'Follows a cable' and phases ["R1", "R3"]; a row written `R1 R3` reads the same

specs.description: A table inside a code fence, or after the first table of the section, is not read
specs.given: an ADR whose `## Features` section holds a fenced block containing a table row `| Fenced | no | |`, then a real table with the row `| Real | yes | |`, then a second table with the row `| Second | no | |`
specs.then: the only feature is 'Real'

specs.description: A Features section with no rows declares that the ADR gives no feature
specs.given: an accepted ADR with a `## Features` section holding only the header and separator rows of the table (and another with the heading and a sentence, no table)
specs.then: declared is true and features is empty, in both; no title row stands in

specs.description: A feature is completed when the phase its row names is built, and accepted when it is not
specs.given: an accepted ADR with `**Built:** R1 on 2026-11-14.`, phases R1 and R2, and rows `| A | a | R1 |` and `| B | b | R2 |`
specs.then: A is completed with built 1 of 1; B is accepted with built 0 of 1

specs.description: A row that names no phase takes the whole ADR: completed only when every unit is built
specs.given: three accepted ADRs, each with the row `| W | w | |`: one with no phases and a `**Built:** F1 on 2026-11-14.` line; one with phases R1 and R2 and only R1 built; one with no phases and no Built line
specs.then: W is completed (1 of 1) in the first, accepted (1 of 2) in the second, accepted (0 of 1) in the third

specs.description: Proposed, retired and unreadable ADRs give their features those states
specs.given: the row `| P | p | |` in a proposed ADR with nothing built, in a superseded ADR, and in an ADR whose status word is 'draft'
specs.when: features_of is called on each with status 'proposed', 'superseded' and 'draft'
specs.then: P is proposed, retired and unknown

specs.description: The status word alone never makes a feature completed, and one built phase of two is not completed
specs.given: an accepted ADR with no Built line and the row `| X | x | |`; and an accepted ADR with phases R1 and R2, R1 built, and the row `| Y | y | R1, R2 |`
specs.then: X is accepted, not completed; Y is accepted with built 1 of 2

specs.description: A completed status builds every phase, as the board reads it
specs.given: an ADR with status 'completed', phases R1 and R2, no Built line, and the row `| Z | z | R2 |`
specs.then: Z is completed with built 1 of 1

specs.description: An ADR with no Features section gives one row: its title, with declared false
specs.given: an accepted ADR ADR-7 titled 'ADR-7: The power read' with a Built line and no `## Features` section
specs.then: declared is false; one feature named 'The power read' (the id prefix is dropped), state completed, declared false, phases []

specs.description: A retired ADR with no Features section gives no row
specs.given: a superseded ADR with no `## Features` section
specs.then: declared is false and features is empty

specs.description: The state of a feature agrees with adr_board::analyze for the same text
specs.given: the ADR texts of S05 to S09
specs.when: features_of and adr_board::analyze are both called on each
specs.then: for every row that names no phase: completed exactly when analyze's state is built, retired exactly when it is retired, unknown exactly when it is unknown, proposed exactly when it is proposed, accepted otherwise (accepted or building)

specs.description: features_of reads nothing but its arguments
specs.given: a current directory that holds no docs/adrs and is not a git repository
specs.when: features_of is called on an ADR text with a Features table
specs.then: it returns the same value as in any other directory; calling it twice returns equal values

specs.description: hexa adr features --json prints every row and a summary by state
specs.given: a project whose docs/adrs holds: a built ADR with two declared features, an accepted ADR with one, a proposed ADR with no Features section, and a superseded ADR with one declared feature
specs.when: `hexa adr features --json` is run in it
specs.then: exit 0; ok is true; features has four rows (the retired one is left out), each with feature, what, state, adr, adr_title, phases, built.done, built.total, declared and released; summary.by_state says completed 2, accepted 1, proposed 1, retired 1; summary.undeclared is 1

specs.description: Rows are ordered by state, then name without regard to case, then ADR id
specs.given: features 'zeta' (completed), 'Alpha' (completed), 'beta' (accepted, in ADR-2 and in ADR-1), 'Gamma' (proposed)
specs.when: `hexa adr features --json` is run, and sort_features is called on the same rows shuffled
specs.then: the order is Alpha, zeta, beta (ADR-1), beta (ADR-2), Gamma, in both

specs.description: --state, --all and --adr choose the rows
specs.given: the project of S14
specs.when: `--state accepted`, `--state accepted --state proposed`, `--state retired`, `--all` and `--adr <the accepted ADR's id>` are each given
specs.then: one row; two rows; the one retired row; five rows; the accepted ADR's one row

specs.description: A state or an ADR that does not exist is refused by name
specs.given: the project of S14
specs.when: `hexa adr features --state shipped --json` and `hexa adr features --adr ADR-0000000000 --json` are run
specs.then: each exits non-zero with ok false and an error carrying code ('bad-state' and 'adr-not-found'), a hint that names the valid states or `hexa adr list`, and field ('state' and 'adr')

specs.description: --md prints a Markdown fact sheet grouped by state
specs.given: the project of S14
specs.then: stdout is Markdown with a heading per state that has rows, in the order completed, accepted, proposed, each followed by a table with the columns Feature, What it does, ADR and Released; the summary counts are stated above the first table; an undeclared row is marked as a title standing in

specs.description: released is the lowest version tag that holds the commit a Built line names
specs.given: a git repository where commit C built a feature (its ADR says `**Built:** F1 on 2026-11-14, <C's short id>.`), tags v0.2.0 and v0.10.0 both contain C, and v0.1.0 does not
specs.then: the row's released is 'v0.2.0' (v0.2.0 is lower than v0.10.0 as numbers)

specs.description: released is null when the commit is unknown, untagged or not named, and for a row that is not completed
specs.given: a completed feature whose Built line names no commit; one whose Built line names a commit that is not in the repository; one whose commit no version tag contains; and an accepted feature
specs.then: released is null on all four; the three completed rows are still completed

specs.description: --md --check passes on a current fact sheet and fails on a stale one
specs.given: the project of S14 with FEATURES.md written by `hexa adr features --md`
specs.when: `hexa adr features --md --check FEATURES.md` is run; then a Built line is added to the accepted ADR and it is run again
specs.then: the first run exits 0; the second exits 1 with the code 'fact-sheet-stale', naming FEATURES.md and the command `hexa adr features --md > FEATURES.md`, and leaves the file as it was

specs.description: The fact sheet carries nothing that changes when no feature does, and a missing file is not a pass
specs.given: the project of S14
specs.when: `hexa adr features --md` is run twice a minute apart and after an unrelated commit; then `--md --check` is given a path that does not exist
specs.then: the three outputs are byte-identical; the check exits 1 with the code 'fact-sheet-missing' and a hint naming the command that writes it

specs.description: A row naming a phase the ADR does not have is unknown, with a warning
specs.given: an accepted ADR with phases R1 and R2 and the row `| Ghost | g | R9 |`
specs.then: Ghost has state unknown and warnings ['unknown-phase']

specs.description: A table with no Feature column makes the ADR undeclared; an empty name is skipped; duplicates are kept and flagged
specs.given: an ADR whose table header is `| Name | What |`; an ADR with rows `|  | nameless | |` and `| Kept | k | |`; an ADR with rows `| Dup | one | |` and `| dup | two | |`
specs.then: the first has warnings ['no-feature-column'], declared false and its title as its one row; the second has warnings ['empty-feature'] and the one feature 'Kept'; the third has both rows, each with warnings ['duplicate-feature']

specs.description: Warnings do not fail the command unless --strict is given
specs.given: a project with the ADR of S23
specs.when: `hexa adr features --json` and `hexa adr features --json --strict` are run
specs.then: the first exits 0 and lists 'unknown-phase' with the ADR's id in warnings; the second prints the same and exits 1

specs.description: extract prints a Features section for an ADR that has none, and writes nothing without --write
specs.given: an accepted ADR with phases R1 and R2, no `## Features` section and a `## Consequences` section; a completion model stubbed to name two features, one for R1
specs.when: `hexa adr features extract <id>` is run, then again with `--write`
specs.then: the first prints a `## Features` section with the table of decision 1 holding the two rows and leaves the file unchanged; the second inserts that section immediately before `## Consequences`; afterwards features_of reads the two rows as declared, with states by decision 2

specs.description: extract refuses an ADR that already declares its features, and cannot call a feature built
specs.given: an ADR that has a `## Features` section; and an accepted ADR with nothing built, with a model stubbed to answer that its feature is 'completed'
specs.when: `hexa adr features extract <id> --write` is run on each
specs.then: the first exits non-zero with the code 'features-declared' and changes nothing; the second writes a table with only the Feature, What it does and Phase columns, and features_of reads the feature as accepted
